# Domain reference: Marketing / Communications

Job family covered: Marketing Officer, Marketing Product Manager, Communications Manager, Digital Manager, Brand Manager, CMO, Growth Manager, Content Manager.

---

## Core competencies (x3)

| Competency | Junior / Marketing Officer | Experienced / Marketing Product Manager | Senior / Marketing Manager | Leadership / CMO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marketing strategy | Executes campaigns, produces content, runs channels. | Builds and manages the marketing plan, defines positioning, manages the mix. | Defines the marketing strategy, aligns with the sales strategy, manages the budget. | Carries the brand and market vision, contributes to corporate strategy, engages with the board. |
| Performance management | Tracks metrics (traffic, leads, engagement). Produces reports. | Analyzes campaign ROI, optimizes channels, manages the funnel. | Defines the strategic KPIs, manages the acquisition/retention budget, forecasts. | Manages marketing performance at group level, arbitrates investments. |
| Customer & market knowledge | Understands the personas, monitors competitors, reports signals. | Conducts market studies, segments, adapts messages by target. | Anticipates trends, defines the insight strategy, feeds the product strategy. | 3-5 year market vision, identifies growth opportunities, positions the brand. |

## Secondary competencies (x2)

| Competency | Description by level |
|---|---|
| Content creation & brand | Junior: produces operational content. Experienced: defines the editorial line, ensures brand consistency. Senior: leads the brand identity, manages agencies. Leadership: carries the corporate brand. |
| Digital & growth | Junior: runs social networks, executes digital campaigns. Experienced: manages acquisition, masters the tools (SEO/SEA/CRM/MA). Senior: defines the digital strategy, leads the transformation. |

## Complementary competencies (x1)

| Competency | Description |
|---|---|
| Internal communication | Newsletter, internal events, internal crisis communication. |
| Press relations & influence | PR management, influencers, external crisis communication. |
| Events | Organizing trade shows, conferences, webinars, product launches. |
| Tools & martech | CRM, marketing automation (HubSpot, Marketo...), analytics (GA, Mixpanel...). |

---

## Recommended role-play scenarios

- **Product launch**: present a fictional product with a constrained budget and deadline. Ask the candidate to build a launch plan (channels, messages, schedule, success metrics). Observe: structure, creativity within constraints, sense of priorities.
- **Campaign analysis**: present the results of a multi-channel campaign with uneven performance. Ask the candidate to analyze, identify the levers and recommend adjustments. Observe: analytical rigor, ability to read data without drowning in it, pragmatism of recommendations.

## Red flags

### Red
- No reference to results or performance measurement
- Purely "creative" discourse with no strategic framework
- Unable to link a marketing action to a business objective

### Orange
- Focus on a single channel with no overall vision
- Difficulty working with sales teams (marketing silo)
- No curiosity about the product or the end customer
